title: Pennsylvania Home Battery Rebates and Incentives 2026
desc: Pennsylvania has no home battery rebate in 2026: no state program, nothing from PPL, and the federal credit ended. Here is what that means and how to decide.
lead: We looked hard, and the honest answer is that Pennsylvania homeowners get no rebate for a home battery in 2026. That does not mean a battery is a bad idea. It means you should buy one for backup power, not for a rebate. Here is what we checked.
cards_heading: What we checked for Pennsylvania batteries
cards_intro: Each card links to the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page.

cards.title: PPL Electric rebates
cards.note: PPL's rebate catalog lists 15 items, from heat pumps to insulation. None is for a battery. We read all of it again on October 6, 2026.

cards.title: PECO rebates
cards.note: PECO's rebate page lists appliance, heating and cooling, new home, water heating and solar rebates. None is for a battery. Its $500 solar rebate is for a first rooftop system only.

cards.title: PA Sunshine Solar Program
cards.note: The old state solar rebate stopped taking applications in 2013. There is no statewide solar or battery rebate today.

cards.title: Federal battery tax credit
cards.note: The 30% federal credit ended for spending after December 31, 2025. A battery installed in 2026 gets nothing from it.

after_cards: We read PECO's rebate program site on October 5, 2026. We could not read Duquesne Light or FirstEnergy Pennsylvania (Penelec and its sister utilities): Duquesne's rebate store says rebates are not available yet, and FirstEnergy's pages would not load. If neither PPL nor PECO is your utility, call yours and ask before you buy.
sections: So why would anyone buy a battery here?

Mostly for outages. A battery keeps your fridge, lights, Wi-Fi, sump pump and furnace fan running when the grid goes down. It does that quietly, with no fuel to store and no engine to service. For a home that loses power during storms, that peace of mind is the real return.

A battery also pairs well with solar. Your panels charge it in the day, and you use that power at night. But with no rebate, the payback from bill savings alone is long. Do not let anyone sell you a battery on a rebate that does not exist.

A standby generator can run a whole house for days if it has fuel. A battery covers a set of key circuits for a shorter time unless solar recharges it. If you need to run central air or an electric furnace through a long outage, a generator may fit better. If you want silent backup for the basics, a battery is cleaner and easier.

Ask any installer to show you, in writing, which circuits the battery will run and for about how long.

The money in Pennsylvania right now is for efficiency. PPL pays for heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, smart thermostats and insulation. PECO has its own heat pump and appliance rebates. Income-qualified homes can get free weatherization from the state Weatherization Assistance Program. Cutting your home's energy use first also means a smaller battery can carry you further in an outage.
Watch out for these sales lines

Be careful if a seller says "the 30% tax credit still applies" for a battery you buy and own, or quotes a "Pennsylvania battery rebate". Ask them to show you the official page. If they lease the system to you instead, the rules are different, so read the contract closely.
claim_heading: How to shop for a battery without a rebate
claim_steps: Decide what you need to keep running in an outage, and for how long.
Call your electric utility and ask if it has any battery or demand-response program for homes.
Get at least two quotes that list the circuits covered and the hours of backup.
Ask each installer how the battery works with your solar, if you have it.
Compare the total cost with a standby generator before you sign.
links: heat pumps, water heaters and insulation
faq: Can I still get the 30% federal tax credit on a battery?
No, not for a battery you buy and install in 2026. The credit ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
Is a home battery worth it in Pennsylvania?
It can be if you lose power often and want quiet backup, or if you pair it with solar. It is hard to justify on bill savings alone without a rebate.
What rebates can I get instead?
PPL and PECO pay for heat pumps, heat pump water heaters, smart thermostats and insulation. Income-qualified households can get free weatherization from the state.
Is there a Pennsylvania home battery rebate in 2026?
We found none. There is no state program, PPL Electric's rebate list has no battery, and PECO's rebate list has none either. Duquesne Light and FirstEnergy Pennsylvania we could not confirm.
Does PECO pay for home batteries?
Not on the PECO pages we read in October 2026. PECO pays $500 for a first rooftop solar system, which does not cover a battery.
